title: Establishing Human Male and Female Models of Cholinergic Neurons via Neurokine-Mediated Differentiation of LA-N-2 and LA-N-5 Neuroblastoma Cells
protocol: Prepare warm medium in sufficient quantity.
Check cell viability and confluency using an inverted microscope.
Collect cells from culture flasks.
Aspirate media from cells.
Resuspend collected cells with warm medium.
Count cells using a hemocytometer.
Seed 200,000 cells per well in 1 mL of medium in a 12-well plate.
Ensure availability of enough culture flasks for the total number of cells needed.
Detach LA-N cells by pipetting along the wall of the flask using a standard 10 mL pipette.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 1,000 × g for 5 min.
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in an appropriate amount of fresh warm medium (e.g., 10 mL).
Count cells and assess viability optionally using Trypan Blue or a digital cell counter.
Dilute cell suspension to yield the desired cell concentration (e.g., 200,000 cells/mL) with fresh warm medium.
Seed cells into 12-well plates using 1 mL of cell-containing medium per well (i.e., in our example, 200,000 cells/well).
Transfer to incubator and incubate for 24 hours at 37°C, 8% CO2.
Pre-warm the stock solution of CNTF.
Visually inspect the condition of the culture using an inverted microscope.
Add pre-warmed aqueous CNTF stock solution to each well to yield a final concentration of 100 ng/mL.
Replace plates into the incubator and minimize disturbance for the duration of the experiment.
Aspirate cell supernatant almost completely from LA-N cells.
Wash cells with 250-500 μL of warm PBS.
Keep PBS in well until all wells have been similarly treated.
Repeat washing step as often as desired, always keeping cells covered to avoid drying out.
Aspirate as much of the supernatant as possible.
Add TRIzol (250 μL) to the well using a micro-pipettor with a slightly larger tip than needed, pipetting up and down until all cells are detached and largely dissolved.
Incubate at 15°C–25°C for 5 min.
Transfer TRIzol containing the cell lysate to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube and place on ice after incubation.
Combine all wells belonging to one sample in the same tube.
Store at −20°C for few days or proceed directly to RNA/protein isolation.
Prepare an ice box.
Prepare chloroform, pure ethanol (ice cold), and 70% ethanol (ice cold) in autoclaved Milli-Q H2O.
Set up microcentrifuge tubes for phase separation and fresh RNase-free tubes for storage of aqueous RNA solution.
Set up a RNA workspace including micro-pipettors, preferably inside a laminar flow hood.
Set centrifuge to 4°C.
Retrieve TRIzol lysate from freezer and allow to thaw on ice.
Add chloroform to TRIzol lysate at 20% of TRIzol volume (200 μL for 1 mL of sample).
Shake manually and vigorously (do not vortex) for 15 s.
Allow each sample to rest for 2–3 min at 15°C–25°C.
Centrifuge samples at 12,000 × g, 15 min, at 4°C.
Retrieve the top, aqueous layer containing RNA and transfer to fresh tube.
Add 1–1.25 ml of pure ethanol (ice cold) to the 500 μL of RNA-containing supernatant.
Mix by inverting and incubate 10–15 min on ice to allow precipitation of RNA.
Centrifuge samples at 12,000 × g, 10 min, at 4°C.
Wash the pellet with 1 mL of 70% ethanol using a vortex apparatus for approximately 10 seconds.
Discard the supernatant and centrifuge the pellet at 7,500 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the tube on ice to an RNase-free section of a laminar flow hood, avoiding any percussion that may disturb the pellet.
Remove as much of the ethanolic supernatant as possible using a suitable RNase-free micro-pipettor.
Keep the microcentrifuge tube open inside the laminar flow hood to allow the pellet to air-dry under close supervision.
Allow most of the residual water to evaporate without letting the pellet dry out completely.
Resuspend the pellet when it becomes translucent at the edges.
Resuspend the pellet in an adequate amount of RNase-free water.
Gently pipette up and down to support resuspension and dissolution of the RNA.
Heat the re-dissolved RNA inside the tube on a heating block for 10 min at 55°C–60°C.
Measure RNA concentration using a Nanodrop 2000 or similar device.
Aliquot and freeze the samples if not proceeding directly to further analysis such as RT-qPCR or next-generation sequencing.
